name: Development
description: For developers, often an AI, building the target application. Gives development areas, implementation records per step of work, project-wide guidelines and sequence diagrams drawn from the code as built.
author: B2IT

personas.name: Development
personas.description: The developer building the target application, usually an AI. Everything here is about the target: modules, classes, endpoints, schema migrations, tests, and how to run them.

node_types.name: Development area
node_types.description: A part of the target application: a backend module or package, a frontend feature, or project-wide. Every development topic sits in exactly one.

node_types.name: Implementation record
node_types.description: What was built for one step of work (for example a migration step or a feature): where it is, how to run it, how it was tested and with what result, and where it departs from the design or from the current behaviour. The record the next step builds on.

fields.name: step
fields.label: Step
fields.hint: The step of work this implements (for example a migration step), by its exact title.

fields.name: backend_changes
fields.label: Backend
fields.hint: Files and classes added or changed in the backend, per module, the endpoints, and the schema migrations added.

fields.name: frontend_changes
fields.label: Frontend
fields.hint: Routes, components and services added or changed in the frontend, and the UI library components used.

fields.name: tests
fields.label: Tests
fields.hint: The integration tests (class and method names), what each proves, how to run them, and the result of the last run.

fields.name: how_to_run
fields.label: How to run it
fields.hint: What to start, in which order, and what to open to see it work.

fields.name: deviations
fields.label: Deviations
fields.hint: Where it departs from the migration design or from the current behaviour, and why.

fields.name: open_issues
fields.label: Open issues
fields.hint: What is unfinished, known to be wrong, or waiting for a decision.

node_types.name: Guideline
node_types.description: A project-wide rule for building the target application: its architecture, conventions, tooling and ways of working. Belongs in the context of every step of work it applies to.

node_types.name: Sequence diagram
node_types.description: How one flow of the application runs through its code: the screen, the frontend services, the API endpoints, the services and the data access, in the order they call each other. One topic per flow a user goes through (placing an order, approving an invoice), drawn from the code as built, so a developer can find their way from a screen to the database and back.

fields.name: subject
fields.label: Flow
fields.hint: The flow it shows, in the user's words: "Placing an order".

fields.name: step
fields.label: Step
fields.hint: The step of work that built it (for example a migration step), by its exact title.

fields.name: overview
fields.label: Overview
fields.hint: Where the flow starts and ends, who goes through it, and what is stored on the way.

fields.name: participants
fields.label: Participants
fields.hint: A table: each participant of the diagram, its file or package, and its part.

fields.name: sequence
fields.label: Sequence
fields.hint: The PlantUML sequence diagram, drawn from the code as built: real class, method and endpoint names, `alt`/`opt`/`loop` for the branches, `==` dividers for the phases. A sentence before it says what it covers.

fields.name: notes
fields.label: Notes
fields.hint: What the diagram leaves out: rules, transactions, error paths, the tests that cover the flow — a subsection each.
